questions.question: What can be found in a vein according to verse 1?
questions.explanation: Job 28:1 says, “Surely there is a vein for the silver.”

questions.question: From what is iron taken?
questions.explanation: Job 28:2 says, “Iron is taken out of the earth.”

questions.question: What does the earth bring forth?
questions.explanation: Job 28:5 says, “As for the earth, out of it cometh bread.”

questions.question: What does the miner search out according to verse 3?
questions.explanation: The verse says that he “searcheth out all perfection.”

questions.question: What precious stones are mentioned in verse 6?
questions.explanation: Job 28:6 says, “The stones of it are the place of sapphires.”

questions.question: What happens to the waters forgotten of the foot?
questions.explanation: Job 28:4 says they “are dried up, they are gone away from men.”

questions.question: According to verse 11, what does the miner bring forth to light?
questions.explanation: Job 28:11 says, “the thing that is hid bringeth he forth to light.”

questions.question: Which creature has not seen the path described in verse 7?
questions.explanation: Job 28:7 says that “the vulture’s eye hath not seen” it.

questions.question: How does the miner act upon the rock?
options: He overturns the mountains by the roots
questions.explanation: Job 28:9 says, “He putteth forth his hand upon the rock; he overturneth the mountains by the roots.”

paragraphs.title: The Limits of Human Searching Before Wisdom

questions.question: Where does verse 12 ask whether wisdom can be found?
questions.explanation: The verse asks, “But where shall wisdom be found?”

questions.question: Is wisdom found in the land of the living?
questions.explanation: Job 28:13 says, “neither is it found in the land of the living.”

questions.question: Can wisdom be gotten for gold?
questions.explanation: Job 28:15 says, “It cannot be gotten for gold.”

questions.question: What does the depth say about wisdom?
questions.explanation: Job 28:14 says, “The depth saith, It is not in me.”

questions.question: What does the sea say?
questions.explanation: The same verse says, “the sea saith, It is not with me.”

questions.question: What is the price of wisdom compared with rubies?
questions.explanation: Job 28:18 says, “the price of wisdom is above rubies.”

questions.question: Which group is listed as unable to equal wisdom?
questions.explanation: Job 28:17 says, “The gold and the crystal cannot equal it.”

questions.question: What does verse 20 repeat as the two questions about wisdom?
options: Who made it and who keeps it?
Whence it comes and where its place is
Why it shines and when it speaks
How it is weighed and sold
questions.explanation: Job 28:20 asks, “Whence then cometh wisdom? and where is the place of understanding?”

questions.question: Name one precious object mentioned in verses 16-19 that cannot equal wisdom.
questions.answer: Any one of: gold of Ophir, precious onyx, sapphire, gold, crystal, coral, pearls, topaz, or pure gold.
questions.explanation: These valuables are all compared with wisdom and shown to be inferior to it.

paragraphs.title: Wisdom Hidden from All Living Beings

questions.question: From whose eyes is wisdom hidden?
questions.explanation: Job 28:21 says wisdom is “hid from the eyes of all living.”

questions.question: What kind of creatures are specifically mentioned as unable to see wisdom?
questions.explanation: The verse says wisdom is “kept close from the fowls of the air.”

questions.question: Who says, “We have heard the fame thereof with our ears”?
questions.explanation: Job 28:22 attributes these words to “Destruction and death.”

questions.question: What have Destruction and death heard?
questions.explanation: They say they have heard “the fame thereof with our ears.”

questions.question: What does “kept close” suggest about wisdom in this passage?
questions.explanation: The phrase indicates that wisdom is concealed from living creatures.

questions.question: Which statement best summarizes verses 21-22?
options: Wisdom is hidden, and even death knows only its report
Wisdom is found in every sea
questions.explanation: The passage says living beings cannot see wisdom, while Destruction and death have only heard of it.

questions.question: What contrast is made between the fowls of the air and Destruction and death?
options: The birds see wisdom, but death rejects it
The birds cannot see wisdom, while Destruction and death have heard its fame
The birds possess wisdom, while death has none
Both groups find wisdom in the sea
questions.explanation: Verse 21 speaks of hiddenness from the fowls, and verse 22 records only a report heard by Destruction and death.

questions.question: Why is the reference to “all living” significant?
options: It emphasizes that no living creature can discover wisdom by sight
It says only humans can find wisdom
It identifies wisdom with physical treasure
questions.explanation: The wording broadens the claim beyond humans: wisdom is hidden from every living creature.

questions.question: Which word in this short passage most directly means a report or renown?
questions.explanation: In verse 22, “fame” refers to the report or renown of wisdom.

paragraphs.title: God Knows the Place of Wisdom

questions.question: Who understands the way of wisdom?
questions.explanation: Job 28:23 says, “God understandeth the way thereof.”

questions.question: What does God see under?
questions.explanation: Verse 24 says God “seeth under the whole heaven.”

questions.question: What does God weigh by measure?
questions.explanation: Job 28:25 says, “he weigheth the waters by measure.”

questions.question: To what does verse 24 say God looks?
options: The bottom of the sea only
questions.explanation: The verse says, “For he looketh to the ends of the earth.”

questions.question: What decree did God make according to verse 26?
options: A decree for the sea to vanish
questions.explanation: Job 28:26 says, “When he made a decree for the rain.”

questions.question: What did God prepare and search out?
questions.explanation: Job 28:27 says, “Then did he see it, and declare it; he prepared it, yea, and searched it out.” The context identifies “it” as wisdom.

questions.question: Which natural forces are mentioned together in verses 25-26?
questions.explanation: The passage mentions the winds, waters, rain, and the lightning of the thunder.

questions.question: What does God’s control over wind and water emphasize?
options: His ordering and governing power over creation
questions.explanation: Measuring the waters and weighing the winds portrays God as sovereign over creation.

questions.question: Which sequence best matches verse 27?
options: He heard it, sold it, and hid it
He saw it, declared it, prepared it, and searched it out
He weighed it, mined it, and exchanged it
He feared it, rejected it, and forgot it
questions.explanation: Job 28:27 gives this sequence: “he saw it, and declare[d] it; he prepared it, yea, and searched it out.”

paragraphs.title: Fear of the Lord and Turning from Evil as Human Wisdom

questions.question: What does the fear of the Lord represent?
questions.explanation: Job 28:28 says, “the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom.”

questions.question: What is understanding according to the verse?
questions.explanation: The verse says, “to depart from evil is understanding.”

questions.question: Whose fear is described?
questions.explanation: The verse specifically speaks of “the fear of the Lord.”

questions.question: What does “depart from evil” mean in context?
questions.explanation: In this moral context, departing from evil means turning away from wrongdoing.

questions.question: How are wisdom and understanding expressed in verse 28?
options: By fearing the Lord and departing from evil
questions.explanation: The verse directly identifies these two responses as wisdom and understanding.

questions.question: Which pair is correctly matched?
options: Fear of the Lord—understanding; departing from evil—wealth
Fear of the Lord—wisdom; departing from evil—understanding
Fear of the Lord—gold; departing from evil—power
Fear of the Lord—death; departing from evil—fame
questions.explanation: Job 28:28 explicitly makes this pairing.

questions.question: What contrast does verse 28 create with the earlier search for earthly treasures?
options: It presents moral obedience as the true human expression of wisdom
It says earthly treasures are worthless in every way
It denies that God knows wisdom
It teaches that miners cannot understand anything
questions.explanation: After describing hidden wisdom, the verse gives a practical human response: reverence for God and rejection of evil.

questions.question: Which statement best captures the verse’s grammatical structure?
options: Fear of the Lord is called wisdom, and departing from evil is called understanding
Wisdom causes fear of the Lord, but evil causes understanding
The Lord fears wisdom, and man departs from understanding
Evil is wisdom, while fear is described as ignorance
questions.explanation: The verse uses two direct identifications: fear of the Lord is wisdom, and departing from evil is understanding.

questions.question: According to Job 28:28, give the two actions or attitudes that show wisdom and understanding.
questions.answer: To fear the Lord and to depart from evil.
questions.explanation: The verse defines wisdom as the fear of the Lord and understanding as departing from evil.
